status: all three arms run; spatial and sublet 2026-10-04 with the gaps closed 2026-10-05, cheribsd-revocation 2026-10-04 with the 12 missing cases built and run 2026-10-05
note: Trigger reaches the bug CONDITION but makes no invalid access (2026-10-11, gdb on the host -O0 build). At vdbeblob.c:420 the cursor is exactly as upstream 8504d37b99 describes: eState=CURSOR_REQUIRESEEK, iPage=-1, and the saved page unpinned in the cache (pPage->pDbPage->nRef=0). No stale read follows, because info.nSize=69 is still set, so getCellInfo returns the cursor's cached cell info instead of parsing the unpinned page; the preupdate hook therefore receives a stale key, which is a correctness defect, not a memory access. The btreeParseCellPtr seen on that same page afterwards comes from accessPayload once the restore has re-pinned it (nRef=1). The lifetime that ended here is the CURSOR'S REFERENCE to the page, which btreeReleaseAllCursorPages dropped while pCur->pPage stayed set: the page is neither freed nor reassigned, so ASan cannot see it by construction. RETRACTED the same day: this note first said a per-reference lifetime at the pager would express it. Measured, that breaks the engine -- pcacheUnpin is a no-op for an in-memory database and SQLite reads page data at nRef==0, so revoking when the reference count reaches zero faults every in-memory case of this corpus in sqlite3Get4byte while reading page 1's header. The boundary a lifetime CAN express is the page RECYCLE, which sublet/sublet-3220000-pagecache.patch covers; this trigger reaches only the unpin, which that patch deliberately leaves alone. Reviewed 2026-10-15 with probe sites 40 and 41 (shared/probe), which replace the gdb session with a re-runnable check and establish more than the trigger: site 40, at the sqlite3BtreeIntegerKey the hook's key comes from, prints eState=3 (CURSOR_REQUIRESEEK) iPage=-1 info.nSize=69, so the bug condition is reached; site 41, in getCellInfo, prints the branch taken and the cursor state at every call -- six parses, all at eState=1 (CURSOR_VALID, ordinary work on pinned pages), and the single call at eState=3 takes the cached branch and never reads the unpinned page. NO TRIGGER CAN REACH AN INVALID ACCESS HERE, and that is structural rather than a property of this one: saveCursorPosition reaches CURSOR_REQUIRESEEK only through saveCursorKey, which for an integer-key table calls sqlite3BtreeIntegerKey and so populates info.nSize, and it clears curFlags but never info.nSize -- so a REQUIRESEEK integer-key cursor always carries valid cached cell info. The operations that do clear info.nSize (moveToRoot, MovetoUnpacked, Next, Previous, Insert) all leave the cursor VALID, so the two conditions are mutually exclusive. What upstream 8504d37b99 fixes, by its own title, is 'invoking the preupdate hook from within sqlite3_blob_write() if the cursor is already invalid': the hook receives a stale key. That is a correctness defect, not a memory-safety one, so this case belongs with the five moved to not-in-scope/ on 2026-10-06 rather than counted as a miss on any arm. Proposed for withdrawal when the review of this corpus ends.
